title: P15.10-C R1: lease heartbeat + bounded claim-time lease lifetime + fenced post-await autonomous commit guard (F1 remediation)
description: R1 remediation on PR #87 (BASE 0e27bc6ee236d82633d4aee321ba9cd264adc0c3): a CEO model call can outlive the 60s lease TTL and nothing revalidated autonomous authority inside the post-await commit transaction. F1-B: scheduler.claim accepts optional max_lifetime_ms (default 300s = P15.10-B compat, min 60s, cap 960s) persisted on the lease and enforced by renew(); TTL stays 60s. F1-A: driver starts a heartbeat ONLY after a valid claim — 20s unref'd interval calling existing scheduler.renew() (each renewal re-proves token/fence/worker-boot/generation/expiry/policy-owner-terms pins); none before claim, no renew inside the 15s no-op window; retryable SQLite contention defers a tick, other faults mark the worker unauthorized and abort settlement; timer always stopped in finally. F1-C: ceoCycle.runCycle takes optional autonomous_commit_guard fired FIRST inside the serialized commit transaction — before re-observe, decision put, workstream decomposition, attempt settle — so mid-call revoke/pause/expiry rolls the whole commit back and the attempt settles REJECTED canonically; runReview forwards it, pass() wires authorityGate, manual callers unchanged. F1-D: driver deps gain ceoTimeoutMs (validated 5s..900s; claim bound=timeout+60s finalization, cap 960s) and pre-admission reconcileStaleAttempts(objectiveId) — restart never re-invokes a STARTED/UNKNOWN attempt; serve wires ceoCliTimeoutMs()+lazy ceoCycle (createDefaultObjectiveOperatingService now returns ceoCycle). Two-connection fencing proven: stale handle cannot renew/settle. No merge, no deploy, driver stays opt-in OFF.
